{
  "dataset_name": "postcutoff_salmonella_serovar_20260401",
  "model_family": "tree",
  "schema_generator": "gemini-3.1-pro-preview",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "green_red_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of the green band (550.90 nm) to the red band (650.80 nm), capturing the relative reflectance peak often associated with specific biological or chemical compositions.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 100.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_ratio",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Tree models can easily split on this ratio to isolate samples with distinct pigmentation or structural characteristics.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "Band_77_W_550.90 / (Band_127_W_650.80 + 1e-5)"
    },
    {
      "name": "nir_red_difference",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Difference between the near-infrared band (800.40 nm) and the red band (650.80 nm), serving as a proxy for structural scattering versus absorption.",
      "value_range": [-4500.0, 200.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_difference",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a direct linear combination that trees can use to separate samples based on their red-edge transition magnitude.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "Band_202_W_800.40 - Band_127_W_650.80"
    },
    {
      "name": "blue_band_intensity_bucket",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Categorize the blue band (451.10 nm) intensity into ordinal buckets (0=low, 1=medium, 2=high, 3=very high) based on typical spectral responses.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 3.0],
      "feature_family": "ordinal_bucket",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Reduces noise and provides a robust ordinal feature that tree models can split on to group similar baseline reflectances.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "is_high_green_peak",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Boolean indicator for whether the green band (550.90 nm) exceeds a high intensity threshold of 1500.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "boolean_indicator",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Creates a hard split for tree models to immediately partition highly reflective samples from darker ones.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.where(Band_77_W_550.90 > 1500.0, 1.0, 0.0)"
    },
    {
      "name": "red_edge_slope",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Approximation of the red-edge slope by taking the difference between 700.70 nm and 650.80 nm.",
      "value_range": [-4500.0, 2400.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_derivative",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures the rate of change in reflectance, which is highly discriminative for biological materials in tree-based splits.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "Band_152_W_700.70 - Band_127_W_650.80"
    },
    {
      "name": "spectral_flatness_nir",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Absolute difference between two NIR bands (800.40 nm and 899.90 nm) to measure the flatness of the spectrum in this region.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 250.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_shape",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Helps the model identify samples with flat vs. sloping NIR responses, providing a nonlinear interaction feature.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.abs(Band_202_W_800.40 - Band_252_W_899.90)"
    },
    {
      "name": "overall_brightness_proxy",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Average intensity across three representative visible bands (blue, green, red) to estimate overall sample brightness.",
      "value_range": [80.0, 4000.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_summary",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a baseline intensity feature, allowing the tree to normalize or condition subsequent splits on overall brightness.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(Band_27_W_451.10 + Band_77_W_550.90 + Band_127_W_650.80) / 3.0"
    },
    {
      "name": "green_peak_prominence",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Measures how much the green band (550.90 nm) stands out above the maximum of the blue (451.10 nm) and red (650.80 nm) bands.",
      "value_range": [-4400.0, 6100.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_shape",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Directly quantifies the local maximum shape, which is a strong nonlinear feature for tree models to exploit.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "Band_77_W_550.90 - np.maximum(Band_27_W_451.10, Band_127_W_650.80)"
    },
    {
      "name": "uv_blue_dropoff",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Difference between the shortest available wavelength (401.00 nm) and the blue band (451.10 nm).",
      "value_range": [-1250.0, 1860.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_difference",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures absorption characteristics in the near-UV region, providing a distinct splitting criterion.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "Band_2_W_401.00 - Band_27_W_451.10"
    },
    {
      "name": "nir_noise_indicator",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Assess whether the NIR region (800-1000nm) exhibits high noise or scattering by evaluating the variance and sudden spikes in the bands, returning a boolean-like indicator.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "data_quality",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Allows the tree to route noisy or highly scattered samples into separate leaf nodes, improving overall robustness.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "red_absorption_depth",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Calculates the depth of the red absorption feature by taking the positive difference between the green peak and the red trough.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 6100.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_shape",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a rectified, non-negative magnitude of absorption that trees can use to threshold specific material properties.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "np.maximum(0.0, Band_77_W_550.90 - Band_127_W_650.80)"
    },
    {
      "name": "normalized_difference_green_red",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Normalized difference between the green (550.90 nm) and red (650.80 nm) bands, scaling the difference by their sum.",
      "value_range": [-1.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "spectral_index",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Offers an illumination-invariant index that tree models can use to split on relative spectral shape regardless of absolute intensity.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true,
      "formula": "(Band_77_W_550.90 - Band_127_W_650.80) / (Band_77_W_550.90 + Band_127_W_650.80 + 1e-5)"
    }
  ]
}
